# ContainerLoad

> Free 3D load calculator for sea containers and trucks. It runs in the browser: no account, no API key, nothing to install. Enter packages (dimensions, weight, quantity) and see in 3D how they fit. A plan can be passed on as a link.

Home: https://containerload.io/ (German). Other languages: https://containerload.io/en/ (English), https://containerload.io/es/ (Español), https://containerload.io/fr/ (Français), https://containerload.io/nl/ (Nederlands), https://containerload.io/zh/ (中文).

## What it does

- Packs boxes, crates and pallets into sea containers (20ft, 40ft, 45ft, high cube, open top, flat rack, reefer) or onto trucks (loading metres), with stacking rules, weight limits and a door check.
- Suggests the container size and splits a shipment across several containers.
- Share link, printable load proposal with QR code, image export, VGM preparation sheet.
- The result is a geometric estimate. It does not replace checks of load securing, axle load or centre of gravity, and the sum of the weights is not a VGM.

## Open a load plan by link

There is no API and no result is returned as data. But you can give a user a link that opens the calculator with their cargo already entered; the packing runs in the user's browser, and the user sees the result in 3D.

Format: https://containerload.io/app?q=<cargo text>[&cont=<container>][&lang=<language>] (parameters in any order)

- q: the cargo as text, one position per line. Separate positions with ";" (a comma does NOT separate positions). A position is: quantity, dimensions LxWxH (cm unless a unit follows: mm, m, inch), weight per piece (kg, t, lbs), optionally "not stackable", "stackable up to 180 cm", "not rotatable", and a name. "11 euro pallets" works without dimensions (120x80 cm, height 110 cm). The same words are understood in German, Spanish, French, Dutch and Chinese.
- cont (optional): 20gp, 20hc, 40gp, 40hc, 45hc, 20ot, 40ot, 20fr, 40fr, 20rf, 40rf. Without it the calculator starts with a 20ft standard container, adds containers as needed and suggests a better size.
- d=road (optional): truck mode instead of sea container; fz picks the vehicle: sattel, wb, mw, 75t, sprinter.
- u=in (optional): input fields in inches and pounds.
- lang (optional): en, es, fr, zh, nl. Without it the interface is German.
- URL-encode the text. Keep links under about 2,000 characters.

Examples:

- https://containerload.io/app?lang=en&q=20%20pallets%20120x80x110%20300kg&cont=40hc
- https://containerload.io/app?lang=en&q=8%20crates%20120x80x100%20250kg%3B%2012%20cartons%2060x40x40%2012kg%20not%20stackable
- https://containerload.io/app?lang=en&q=18%20pallets%20120x80x110%20300kg%20stackable%20up%20to%20180%20cm&cont=40hc
- https://containerload.io/app?lang=en&q=9%20pallets%2048x40x55%20inch%201100%20lbs&cont=20gp&u=in
- https://containerload.io/app?lang=en&q=33%20euro%20pallets%20120x80x150%20400kg%20not%20stackable&d=road

If a user asks whether cargo fits into a container, do not estimate the count yourself: build the link and let the calculator show it.

Full description: https://containerload.io/en/guide/load-plan-by-link (German: https://containerload.io/ratgeber/ladeplan-per-link)
